label: Tier bands
description: How early, cheap and complex a unit is. Tiers cap the number of keys: every button except primary fire and movement (secondary weapon, active abilities, toggles, deploys, key-bound movement, ultimate). The cap is a maximum, not a target, and counts innate abilities only. Universal keys that every unit shares never count: E interact (enter or leave a seat, pick up), hold F shake off anything attached to you, hold X bail out of a vehicle, 1-3 switch seat, middle mouse ping, and G for a transport's driver to evict passengers. A signature fired with primary fire counts as primary fire only when it is the unit's primary weapon. For source units the tier comes from tech gating alone; games without tech tiers record none. Some games use 'tier' for upgraded versions of the same vehicle (Foxhole, Halo Wars): record those as upgrades, not tiers.

terms.label: T1
terms.description: Early: cheap, available from the start, simple and readable.
terms.source_rule: Built from a basic production building with no extra tech.

terms.label: T2
terms.description: Mid: needs one tech step; stronger or more specialised.
terms.source_rule: Needs one tech building or upgrade beyond the basics.

terms.label: T3
terms.description: Late: top tech, elites and super-heavies. May carry an ultimate.
